newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco stocks drop after settlement.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco stocks drop after settlement.

text.p: Tobacco company stocks fell Monday in their first full day of trading since Friday's announcement of the $368.5 billion national litigation settlement.
The decline bucked the predictions made by most industry analysts recently that tobacco shares would rise after a settlement.

Philip Morris Cos. Inc., one of the most heavily traded stocks on the New York Stock Exchange on Monday, fell $1.875 to $43.625 in afternoon trading. More than 11 million shares changed hands in consolidated trading.
Also on the NYSE, RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. fell $1.625 to $33.375, Loews Corp. fell $2.125 to $101.25, and UST Inc. lost 75 cents to $28.25.
The American Stock Exchange's Tobacco Index .TOB was down 7.10, or 2.23 percent, at 311.49 points.

The settlement announced Friday has left enough doubt about the deal's ability to be passed by Congress and the White House that many investors have yet to feel the shares are free and clear from harm, analysts said Monday.

"We're probably going to go through a period over the next few weeks when there's not going to be any good news. You won't really have any bad news either, but you will have some bashing of the deal," said David Adelman at Morgan Stanley.

For the next several months, "there won't be any clear signs that the bill (to approve the settlement in Congress) is making progress. I think the legislation is going to pass, and that it's going to lead to higher (stock) prices toward the end of the year," Adelman said.
The boost in share prices anticipated from the deal could fizzle "until there is something to which you can attach some incremental hope," Adelman said.
Other analysts were equally sanguine about the settlement's prospect for passage, despite the prevalence of detractors outside Wall Street.
Both Smith Barney's Martin Feldman and Paine Webber's Emanuel Goldman expect the settlement's essential elements will get Congressional approval.
Another Wall Street firm, Oppenheimer & Co., raised its target for the stock prices of three major cigarette makers, based on the assumption that the settlement passes in its current state.

Oppenheimer analyst Roy Burry said the targets also assume the federal government will pass a 20-cent-a-pack increase in the federal excise tax. The Senate Finance Committee gave its nod on Thursday before passing the measure to the House of Representatives.
Oppenheimer predicts Philip Morris stock will rise to $64 a share, that RJR will rise to $48, and that B.A.T Industries Plc's American shares will rise to $29.
